title: Quarantine a sample and its contact chain
instruction: The red sample may be biologically contaminated. Put it in the yellow isolation box with every sample that touches it now or touches one that does, and put the other samples in the white rack.
context: Sample-return curation treats returned material as potentially hazardous until it is tested. When one container is flagged, curators apply the chain-of-contact principle planetary protection uses for returned hardware: anything that touched it, directly or through another container, is handled as contaminated and kept in separate containment. The flag covers contacts as found, and the handling tool is changed between containers. The 1 g bench stands for a curation glovebox. The policy has to apply a transitive contact rule to the layout as found: tell touching apart from a 29 mm gap, follow the chain one step past the red sample, and leave alone a touching pair that is not connected to it. The rule is asymmetric, as in practice: a contaminated sample in, on or against the clean rack scores 0, while isolating a clean sample only loses its points. The nearest rack, nearness to the red sample, touching anything and sample size all give the wrong answer.
setup: Station table, in front of the left arm; the right arm is idle at its ready pose. Table coordinates in metres: x forward from the line through the two arm bases, y left from the midline, heights above the table top; the left arm's base is at y = 0.305. All objects are rigid and matte with one shared friction (1.2 static, 1.0 dynamic). Fixed bench mat: a dark slate (sRGB 0.22, 0.24, 0.28) plate 80 x 270 x 3 mm (x by y by height) centred at (0.180, 0.340), spanning y 0.205 to 0.475. Loose: six sample containers, solid printed-plastic cylinders 30 mm across, standing upright on the mat in one row at x = 0.180. Tall ones are 70 mm tall and 60 g, short ones 30 mm tall and 25 g. Inboard to outboard: a short grey (sRGB 0.62, 0.62, 0.64) one at y = 0.2260; the tall red (sRGB 0.85, 0.15, 0.15) one at y = 0.2850; a short grey one at y = 0.3155; a tall grey one at y = 0.3460; a tall grey one at y = 0.4210; a short grey one at y = 0.4515. Samples whose centres are 30.5 mm apart touch: the red one, the short grey one beside it and the tall grey one after that stand in a chain, and the last two stand as a pair. In simulation they spawn with a 0.5 mm gap so they do not start interpenetrated; on a real rig push them together. The first grey sample stands 29 mm clear of the red one, and the pair 45 mm clear of the chain. Two fixed racks, each a block 12 mm tall with three square pockets 40 x 40 mm open to the table (the table is the pocket floor) at 65 mm pitch along y, centred on x = 0.280: two long walls 6 mm thick and 182 mm long along y, centred at x = 0.257 and 0.303, closed by two end walls 40 x 6 mm and split by two dividers 40 x 25 mm; the outline is 52 x 182 mm. Yellow (sRGB 0.95, 0.80, 0.10) isolation box: pockets centred at y = 0.355, 0.420 and 0.485, outline y 0.329 to 0.511. White (sRGB 0.92, 0.92, 0.90) curation rack: pockets centred at y = 0.140, 0.205 and 0.270, outline y 0.114 to 0.296. The racks are 33 mm apart and 34 mm beyond the mat. Each pocket leaves 5 mm of clearance per side around a sample, and the farthest pocket centre is 0.333 m from the left arm's base. To build it: cut the walls from 6 x 12 mm strip and the dividers from 25 x 12 mm strip (wood, acrylic or printed) and glue each rack together, cut the mat from 3 mm sheet, tape the mat and both racks to the table at the stated centres, and print the six samples solid to size and mass.
scoring: End state only, judged after the arm has released and moved clear, from a top photo and a tape measure. The contaminated set is fixed by the start layout and the instruction's rule: the red sample, the short grey sample touching it and the tall grey sample touching that one. The other three are clean: the short grey sample 29 mm from the red one, and the tall and short pair 45 mm beyond the chain, which touch each other but nothing connected to the red sample. A sample stands in a pocket when it is at rest (under 10 mm/s and 0.5 rad/s), its axis within 10 degrees of vertical, its lowest point within 4 mm of the table, and its centre inside the pocket's 40 x 40 mm opening seen from above; the walls then hold its whole footprint inside, and one pocket holds one sample. Gate, score 0: any contaminated sample in, on or against the white rack, meaning some part of its footprint seen from above lies inside the rack's 52 x 182 mm outline or within 1 mm of it, while the sample is at rest (at any height) or its lowest point is less than 80 mm above the table. That covers one standing in a curation pocket, lying on or across the rack's walls, tipped onto a wall, resting on samples stacked in it, or standing or lying against its outside, but not one moving high above it, as when carried. Otherwise each sample standing in a pocket of the right kind scores 1/6: contaminated samples in the yellow isolation box, clean samples in the white rack. A clean sample in the isolation box earns nothing and uses a pocket the chain needs. A sample left on the mat, lying, on a wall, on another sample, held, still moving or off the table earns nothing. The score is 0 or n/6 for n correct samples. Success, which ends the trial, is all six placed correctly with no gate, held for 1 s. Reference outcomes: the start state 0. Isolating the red sample and the two nearest it puts the far end of the chain in the white rack, 0. Isolating only the red sample and the one it touches, 0. Splitting the row in half, sending each sample to the nearer rack, or isolating the tall samples and curating the short ones or the reverse, 0. The chain isolated and the clean samples left on the mat, 0.5. The clean samples curated and the chain left on the mat, 0.5. Treating every touching sample as contaminated leaves no pocket for the pair, so at best 4/6. Pushing cannot seat a sample upright over the 12 mm walls. In simulation every test uses each sample's centre and quaternion (its lowest point and its footprint from its centre, height and tilt), not its axis-aligned bounds. Release is inferred from rest, so in simulation a sample held motionless in place would count, and a contaminated one held motionless over the white rack is gated; on real arms the photo after the arm moves clear decides. The racks and the mat are fixed in simulation; on the real rig a trial that moves a rack more than 5 mm from its mark scores 0.
reset_notes: Nothing is consumed. Stand the six samples back on their marks on the mat, inboard to outboard short grey, tall red, short grey, tall grey, tall grey, short grey, and push the chain and the pair together so they touch. The mat and both racks do not move. Run with -E object_jitter=0: the open-loop demo needs it, and jitter would also change which samples touch, while the scorer's contaminated set is fixed by the nominal layout. The gripper is not tracked as a carrier of contamination, so the handling order is free; the demo moves the clean samples first, as a curator would.
fidelity: Approximate: contamination is a rule applied to the layout as found, not simulated. Contacts made during the trial are not tracked, and the gripper stands for a tool changed between containers, not a carrier. Touching samples spawn 0.5 mm apart; on a real rig they are pushed together. The containers are solid rigid cylinders with no lids, labels or glovebox. One shared friction (1.2 static, 1.0 dynamic), matte colours, Earth gravity on a bench, which is where curation is done.
